Remember one point: language is the key, and literature is the world behind the door. Foreign language teachers give students the key and guide them as they open the door.

It does not suit people who want stability without research. Postsecondary faculty face demanding reviews, and both teaching and research must be strong. Enrollment changes also affect positions in less commonly taught languages.

A common path is: bachelor's degree in a target language or comparative literature -> graduate study in China or abroad -> publications and teaching experience -> postsecondary faculty application -> begin as a lecturer -> pass contract reviews and seek promotion -> advance toward program leadership or professorship.

This career suits people who love languages and literature and can sustain focused study. It is a strong fit if you will read more than a dozen papers for one literature class and enjoy discussing cultural differences and shared experience with students.

They research the literature and culture of target-language countries, advise undergraduate and graduate theses, and support program development and international exchange.

People who love language and literature and accept the slow work of research can find satisfaction in both teaching and scholarship.
